projects.projectName: Vivli - AI Form Check Validation & Agentic Chat Automation

predictedRisks.riskTitle: Contract-to-delivery baseline misalignment may delay acceptance and go-live governance
predictedRisks.riskDescription: The project is likely to encounter a material delivery governance risk because planned acceptance, regression, deployment, training, and hypercare activities extend well beyond the contractual end date of September 11, 2026, with no documented amendment or formal extension approval. This creates a high probability of delayed approvals, disputed milestone completion, or constrained decision-making during the transition into PAT, deployment, and hypercare.
predictedRisks.rootCause: Original SOW defined a 16-week milestone structure through September 11, 2026, but current execution plan includes additional phases and a projected end date of October 30, 2026 without documented contract realignment.
triggerConditions: No approved contract amendment or revised baseline before PAT begins
Milestones after September 11, 2026 require client approval under the original SOW
Deployment, regression, or hypercare activities continue outside contractual coverage
Payment milestone timing is challenged due to shifted milestone definitions

potentialImpact.schedule: PAT, regression, deployment, or sign-off decisions may be delayed by 2-6 weeks due to approval or governance hold points
potentialImpact.cost: Potential fixed-price exposure and unplanned effort if post-contract work proceeds without commercial alignment
potentialImpact.quality: Late governance decisions can compress regression and release readiness activities
potentialImpact.customer: Stakeholder confidence may decline if timeline and contractual expectations diverge
potentialImpact.operations: Go-live readiness and hypercare support commitments may remain unclear

supportingPatterns: Historical Vivli risk recorded regression and extended PAT being added after initiation and outside the original SOW
Historical mitigation was weakly evidenced and did not prevent recurrence
Current timeline again shows PAT, regression, deployment, and hypercare outside the contractual baseline

predictedRisks.estimatedResolutionTime: Medium (1-3 weeks) if escalated immediately; longer if deferred into PAT
mitigationPlan: Execute formal contract amendment or approved baseline reset through October 30, 2026
Map actual phases to revised milestone/payment definitions
Establish explicit go/no-go governance criteria for PAT exit, code freeze, deployment, and hypercare
Document ownership for approvals across Vivli and Ascendion leadership
recommendations: Escalate this as a steering-level governance risk immediately
Do not allow PAT to proceed without documented commercial/timeline alignment
Publish a revised integrated milestone plan with approval dates and decision authorities
Separate delivery confidence from contractual readiness in status reporting
predictedRisks.reasoning: This risk is directly supported by the SOW end date of September 11, 2026, the WSR timeline continuing through October 30, 2026, schedule status marked UNDER REVIEW, and explicit extension analysis showing no formal approval documented. Historical evidence shows this exact governance drift pattern already emerged in the same Vivli delivery context and was not durably resolved.
monitoringIndicators: Status of contract amendment / change approval
Milestone acceptance disputes or delayed approvals
Escalations on post-September resource or payment coverage

projectIndicators: PAT, Regression, Deployment, Training, and Hypercare are scheduled outside contract baseline
Formal extension approval is NOT DOCUMENTED
historicalReferences: Historical risk R01: regression testing and extended PAT were added after initiation and not part of original SOW

predictedRisks.riskTitle: Unresolved client-owned dependencies may block Sprint 5 completion and production readiness
predictedRisks.riskDescription: The project is likely to face near-term execution slippage because multiple high-severity client-owned dependencies remain unresolved late in the lifecycle, threatening Sprint 5 completion, PAT readiness, monitoring readiness, and integrated workflow completion.
predictedRisks.rootCause: Critical delivery items depend on Vivli-side decisions, provisioning, and internal actions, including escalation workflow refinement, Azure monitoring/alert process confirmation, automation testing environment provisioning, and Guru Card fit assessment.
triggerConditions: Chat-based escalation requirements remain unresolved before Sprint 5 build window
Dedicated automation testing environment is not provisioned before PAT
Azure monitoring and escalation alerting process is not confirmed before production-readiness review
Guru Card fit assessment remains open and affects chatbot integration decisions

potentialImpact.schedule: Sprint 5 and PAT entry may slip by 1-3 weeks due to blocked stories and incomplete readiness
potentialImpact.cost: Additional coordination, rework, and extended resource effort may be required
potentialImpact.quality: Testing may proceed with incomplete integration or reduced environment fidelity
potentialImpact.customer: Business demos and acceptance confidence may weaken if critical workflows are partially implemented
potentialImpact.operations: Monitoring, alerting, and support readiness for go-live may be incomplete

supportingPatterns: Historical Vivli risk recorded sprint slippage due to broader scope and client cloud environment dependencies
Current project again shows dependency-driven delays as an identified delivery pattern
Historical mitigation did not eliminate systemic dependency risk

predictedRisks.estimatedResolutionTime: Short-Medium (1-4 weeks) depending on client response speed
mitigationPlan: Assign dated closure commitments for each high-severity dependency
Escalate unresolved items to steering/forum with explicit impact statements
Prepare fallback paths for non-blocking partial delivery where feasible
Create dependency burn-down tracking through Sprint 5 and PAT entry
recommendations: Treat unresolved dependencies as critical-path items rather than routine RAID tracking
Require weekly executive confirmation on Vivli-owned actions
Prioritize environment and monitoring readiness ahead of lower-criticality enhancements
Define minimum viable acceptance criteria if one dependency remains late
predictedRisks.reasoning: There are four explicitly documented high-severity dependencies still in progress at Week 11, while only one sprint remains before PAT. Dependency risk is rated high in the current intelligence, and the project pattern explicitly identifies dependency-driven delays. Historical evidence from the same client context shows this dependency type has already caused sprint delay.
monitoringIndicators: Closure date for escalation requirements refinement
Provisioning status of automation testing environment
Approval status of Azure monitoring/alert process

projectIndicators: Automation testing environment is required for comprehensive testing and PAT
Azure monitoring/alert process is required for production readiness
historicalReferences: Historical risk R02: sprint delivery slipped due to broader scope and client cloud environment dependencies

predictedRisks.riskTitle: PAT may produce acceptance delays due to feedback volume and residual quality gaps
predictedRisks.riskDescription: The project is likely to experience acceptance-cycle delay during PAT because the current delivery model is highly feedback-driven, significant PAT early verification feedback has already emerged, and UI/UX and front-end testing concerns remain active late in the build cycle.
predictedRisks.rootCause: Substantial feedback and defect/enhancement intake across early access reviews, a meaningful share of UI-related bugs, and late front-end automation strengthening create a risk that formal PAT uncovers more issues than can be closed within the planned acceptance window.
triggerConditions: Sprint 5 backlog remains heavy with bug fixes and enhancement feedback entering PAT
UI/UX defects continue to represent a significant share of open issues
Client feedback turnaround during PAT is slower than planned
Critical or medium defects discovered in integrated workflow, role-based access, or chatbot behaviors

potentialImpact.schedule: PAT completion and PAT sign-off may slip by 1-3 weeks, compressing regression and deployment
potentialImpact.cost: Additional QA and remediation cycles may increase effort consumption
potentialImpact.quality: Compressed fix/verify cycles may allow residual defects into regression or release
potentialImpact.customer: User confidence may decline if usability or workflow defects persist during acceptance testing
potentialImpact.operations: Production-readiness may be delayed if unresolved defects affect support workflow, access control, or monitoring behavior

supportingPatterns: Historical Vivli risk showed customer feedback timing could impact subsequent sprint validation and implementation
Current WSR reports significant PAT feedback issues and fixes being carried into current sprint
Historical evidence shows review-driven execution without sufficient schedule buffer repeatedly affects downstream phases

predictedRisks.estimatedResolutionTime: Medium (2-4 weeks) depending on defect severity and client review turnaround
mitigationPlan: Define PAT defect triage thresholds before PAT start
Separate true defects from enhancement requests to protect acceptance scope
Run focused UI/UX review and integrated workflow walkthroughs before PAT entry
Increase daily defect aging and retest monitoring during PAT
Pre-align business-critical acceptance criteria with Vivli reviewers
recommendations: Use a strict severity-based acceptance model during PAT
Freeze discretionary enhancements before PAT unless they are acceptance blockers
Expand pre-PAT integrated demo and rehearsal coverage for both use cases
Track client response SLA for PAT reviews and escalations
predictedRisks.reasoning: The WSR explicitly notes significant PAT early verification feedback, a dedicated PAT feedback agenda, UI-heavy bug mix, and front-end testing coverage concerns. PAT is planned for 15 days on a compressed critical path with little buffer. Historical Vivli evidence shows review timing and feedback volume materially affect validation cadence and downstream implementation.
monitoringIndicators: PAT feedback volume and closure rate

projectIndicators: Received feedback from PAT early verification testing requiring fixes
Good percentage of bugs are UI-related from usability standpoint
Automation resource started only in Sprint 4
PAT and regression are both on critical path with limited buffer
historicalReferences: Historical risk R03: delayed customer feedback could impact subsequent sprint validation and implementation

predictedRisks.riskTitle: Late-stage technical changes may introduce regression before PAT exit
predictedRisks.riskDescription: The project is likely to face a technical stability risk because Sprint 5 includes multiple late-stage changes with cross-cutting impact—GPT-5 Mini migration, MSAL/RBAC completion, escalation workflow integration, test coverage completion, and DevOps IaC sign-off—immediately before formal PAT and downstream regression.
predictedRisks.rootCause: Several technically meaningful changes are clustered into the final sprint before acceptance testing, leaving limited stabilization time if any change affects behavior, security, integration, or environment consistency.
triggerConditions: GPT-5 Mini migration changes model behavior or output consistency
MSAL/RBAC implementation surfaces authorization defects in admin workflows
Escalation workflow integration introduces defects across chat and human-review routing
Unit/integration coverage gaps remain unresolved by Sprint 5 end

potentialImpact.schedule: Additional remediation and retesting could delay PAT exit or extend regression by 1-2 weeks
potentialImpact.cost: Extra engineering and QA effort may be required for rollback, tuning, or retesting
potentialImpact.quality: Model behavior, access control, or integration defects may reduce reliability and acceptance confidence
potentialImpact.customer: Business stakeholders may perceive instability if late changes affect expected demo or PAT outcomes
potentialImpact.operations: Deployment readiness may weaken if environment, alerting, or auth controls are not stable

supportingPatterns: Historical patterns show late-cycle dependency and feedback pressure reducing stabilization time
Current project already exhibits compressed late-stage execution and reactive mitigation behavior
No directly equivalent historical technical migration risk was evidenced, so confidence is moderated

predictedRisks.estimatedResolutionTime: Short-Medium (1-3 weeks) depending on defect severity and rollback readiness
mitigationPlan: Sequence Sprint 5 changes by production criticality and testability
Execute targeted regression suites immediately after each major change
Prepare rollback/fallback plan for GPT-5 Mini migration
Validate RBAC through role-matrix-based test scenarios before PAT
Require IaC sign-off before release-readiness commitment
recommendations: Do not batch all late technical changes into a single validation event
Use feature-complete readiness gates before PAT start
Prioritize stability over enhancement closure in final sprint
Add explicit technical readiness review covering model, security, and integration behavior
predictedRisks.reasoning: Sprint 5 scope explicitly includes GPT-5 Mini migration, MSAL/RBAC, escalation workflow integration, coverage completion, and IaC sign-off. These are late, coupled changes occurring just before PAT in a schedule already under pressure. While technical feasibility is assessed as generally feasible, these final-sprint changes materially increase the chance of regression and retest churn.
monitoringIndicators: Sprint 5 scope burn-down against change categories
RBAC defect count and role-matrix pass rate
Integration test pass trend after late-stage changes

projectIndicators: Sprint 5 includes GPT-5 Mini migration and validation
historicalReferences: Historical patterns indicate compressed, feedback-driven late-cycle execution rather than direct prior migration evidence
